name: India–Pakistan
value: Indus treaty in abeyance; no LoC strike found
summary: India keeps the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance; Pakistan bars Indian aircraft to 24 Nov; no cross-border strike
state: India continues to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, despite a 31 Aug ruling by the Court of Arbitration in The Hague that found no grounds for the suspension. Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian-registered aircraft runs to 24 Nov (Dawn). No ceasefire violation, cross-border strike, mobilisation or major attack with blame assigned was found as of 17 Nov; the continuing treaty suspension keeps Watch.
for_you: Flights between Europe and India may still route around Pakistani airspace, adding time. Travellers to the region should follow FCDO travel advice, particularly near the Line of Control.
rubric_hit: Treaty suspension continuing (Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance) = Watch; no cross-border strikes
why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
